# Noxel demo assets

**Generated by `noxel-gen`. Do not hand-edit anything in this directory** —
every file here is overwritten on the next run, and `noxel-gen verify` fails
the build when a file no longer matches the generator.

```sh
cargo run -p noxel-gen -- generate --force   # rewrite the whole tree
cargo run -p noxel-gen -- verify             # check it against the generator
cargo run -p noxel-gen -- preview            # contact sheet of the textures
cargo run -p noxel-gen -- list               # what is generated, and how big
```

## Units

One tile is 16x16 pixels, one world unit and one metre. A character cell is
16x24 pixels and stands 1.0 x 1.5 world units. All art is authored against the
24-colour palette in `config/palette.json`; index == colour id, and no pixel
outside that list is ever written.

## config/

Data files. `palette.json` is the fixed 24-colour palette, in index order:
colour id 0 is `shadow`, id 4 is `grass_dark`, and so on. Every texture in
this tree is drawn only from these colours, and every colour is used by at
least one material ramp.

## textures/

PNG atlases, all nearest-neighbour pixel art with hard alpha (no partial
coverage anywhere). `terrain.png` is 16 ground tiles of 16x16 in a single row,
`buildings.png` is 12 wall/roof/floor tiles of 16x16 in a single row,
`characters.png` is a 5x4 grid of 16x24 cells (four walk frames per direction
plus an idle cell, rows in the order down/left/right/up), and `props.png` is a
single 24-pixel-tall row of prop cells: three 24x24 tree-canopy frames followed
by 11 cells of 16x16.

## tilesets/

Tile definitions: id, name, `uv` region, gameplay flags and stack height. Tile
ids are unique across both files (terrain 0-15, buildings 16-27), so a prefab
voxel can name any tile with one number. `uv` regions are in texture pixels and
never overlap.

## prefabs/

Building blocks for the world generator: a `voxels` list (grid position, tile
id and the tile name for readability), `props`, `spawns` (a door, a shopkeeper,
a patrol point) and `occluders`. Sizes are in tiles: `house_small` is 5x4 tiles
and three tiles tall. Every prefab is structurally validated by the generator:
no voxel outside its bounds, no two voxels in the same cell, and every building
has a door on its perimeter with a walkable floor behind it.

## sprites/

Sprite sheet descriptions: the texture to read, the default frame, the pivot,
the display size in world units and the frame list. `characters.json` also
carries an `animations` index that groups the frames into `walk_down`,
`idle_up` and the rest, with each animation's loop flag and duration.

## world/

The demo world configuration the `town-demo` example reads: seed, size, biome
hints, towns, roads and named points of interest. See `world/README.md` for the
schema. Units are tiles, and one tile is one metre.

## Files

24 generated files, all of them listed in `manifest.json` with
their kind — the manifest lists itself too, so the manifest and the directory
hold the same set. The one file that is *not* an asset is `preview.png`: it is
a contact sheet written on demand by `noxel-gen preview` for eyeballing the
art, and it is deliberately kept out of the manifest.
